fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Optional prompt for layer separation. - When a prompt is provided, the model separates the specified elements based on the prompt - When no prompt is provided, the model automatically identifies the main elements in the image - Supports using `<bbox>x1 y1 x2 y2</bbox>` to precisely specify element positions, recommending the use of normalized coordinates in the 0-1000 range - Length: 4–5000 characters
fields.example: Separate the title text <bbox>179 58 809 197</bbox> and the parrot <bbox>330 274 641 991</bbox> into independent layers

fields.name: image_url
fields.description: The source image URL for layer separation. - Must upload exactly 1 image - Supported formats: PNG, JPEG. - Image size must not exceed 30 MB - Total pixel range is 262,144-36,000,000 - Aspect ratio range is 1:16-16:1

fields.name: size
fields.description: Resolution level of the output image. The base image maintains the aspect ratio of the input image, and each separated layer maintains the aspect ratio of the corresponding element in the original image. - `auto`: Automatically selected based on the input image size - `1K`: 1K resolution level - `1.5K`: 1.5K resolution level - `2K`: 2K resolution level

fields.name: output_format
fields.description: Output format of the base image. This parameter only controls the base image format; all separated layers are fixed to output as PNG.

## Create Task

Use this endpoint to create a new image generation task. Provide a text prompt, and optionally include image URLs as visual references.

Output: one JPEG image per task. The output format cannot be set; do not rely on the file extension in the result URL.

- Set `image_urls` to an empty array or omit it for pure text-to-image generation. Up to 10 images are supported.
- Supported aspect ratios: `1:1`, `1:4`, `1:8`, `2:3`, `3:2`, `3:4`, `4:1`, `4:3`, `4:5`, `5:4`, `8:1`, `9:16`, `16:9`, `21:9`, `auto`.

## Create Task

Use this endpoint to create a GPT Image 2.6 Flare text-to-image task.

### GIF animation

| Parameter | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `frame_count` | `9` | Integer 2–16. |
| `frame_duration_ms` | `200` | Duration per frame in integer milliseconds. Minimum 20, rounded to 10 ms. |
| `size` | `auto` | Per-frame pixel size. Width and height must be multiples of 16. Omit or pass `auto` for 512×512. Do not pass ratio names such as `1:1`. |

Frames are first packed into a sprite sheet: 2–8 frames use 4×2, 9 frames use 3×3, 10–12 frames use 4×3, 13–16 frames use 4×4. Rows and columns may be swapped to get a closer-to-square layout. The full sheet must have each side ≤ 3840, total pixels ≤ 8,294,400, and long/short side ratio ≤ 3:1, otherwise the request returns 400.

::: warning[]
`512x512` works for all 2–16 frames; `768x768` supports at most 12 frames. `1024x1024` exceeds the per-side sheet limit even with only 2 frames.
:::

fields.description: Aspect ratio. Optional, default `auto`. fields.description: Background. Optional, default `auto`. Transparent background is only supported with `png` / `webp` / `gif`. - `transparent`: transparent background, useful for product cut-outs, icons and stickers. `output_format` must be `png` or `webp` - `opaque`: always a solid background - `auto` (default): the model decides

fields.name: output_format
fields.description: Output format. Optional, default `png`. Passing `jpg` is treated as `jpeg`. Supported: `png`, `jpeg`, `webp`, `gif`, `svg`. - Transparent background is only supported with `png` / `webp` - For `gif`, use `size` / `frame_count` / `frame_duration_ms`; do not send `svg` - For `svg`, send `svg.model`; do not send the GIF fields

fields.description: JPEG / WebP compression, 0–100. Optional. Send only when `output_format` is `jpeg` or `webp`. Do not include this field for other formats.

fields.name: size
fields.description: GIF **per-frame** pixel size. Send only when `output_format=gif`. Width and height must both be multiples of 16. Optional, default `auto` (currently equivalent to `512x512`). Do not pass ratio names such as `1:1`. Do not send for non-gif. Frames are first packed into a sprite sheet: 2–8 frames use 4×2, 9 frames use 3×3, 10–12 frames use 4×3, 13–16 frames use 4×4. Rows and columns may be swapped to get a closer-to-square layout. The full sheet must have each side ≤ 3840, total pixels ≤ 8,294,400, and long/short side ratio ≤ 3:1, otherwise the request returns 400. - `512x512` works for all 2–16 frames - `768x768` supports at most 12 frames - `1024x1024` exceeds the per-side sheet limit even with only 2 frames

## Create Task


Use this endpoint to create a GPT Image 2.6 Economy image-to-image (image editing) task. Try it online and see pricing on the [GPT Image 2.6 API page](https://kie.ai/gpt-image-2-6).


GPT Image 2.6 Economy is the cost-efficient GPT Image 2.6 variant. It generates at 1K only, with a smaller set of aspect ratios and output formats. For faster iteration with more sizes, use GPT Image 2.6 Flare; for more detail and tighter consistency across edits, use GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst.


### Parameter tips


- `aspect_ratio` supports `auto`, `1:1`, `16:9`, `9:16`, `3:2`, `2:3`, `21:9`, `4:3`.

- `output_format` supports `png` only (default).

- `background`: `transparent`, `opaque` or `auto` (default `auto`).

- Pass up to 16 images in `input_urls` and refer to them by order in the prompt (for example, "the product from image 1 on the background from image 2").

## Overview

Generate images from input images using the GPT Image 1.5 Image To Image model. This model allows you to edit or modify existing images with text prompts. The process consists of two steps: create a generation task and query task status and results.

## File Upload Requirements

Before using this API, you need to upload your image files:

<Steps>
<Step title="Upload Image">
  Use the File Upload API to upload your source image.

  <Card title="File Upload API" icon="lucide-upload" href="/file-upload-api/quickstart">
    Learn how to upload images and get file URLs
  </Card>
</Step>

<Step title="Get File URL">
  After upload, you'll receive a file URL that you can use in the `input_urls` parameter.
</Step>
</Steps>

:::warning
- Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP
- Maximum file size: 10MB
- Maximum 16 input URLs per request
- Images should be appropriate and follow usage guidelines
:::

## Query Task Status

After submitting a task, use the unified query endpoint to check progress and retrieve results:

<Card title="Get Task Details" icon="lucide-search" href="/market/common/get-task-detail">
  Learn how to query task status and retrieve generation results
</Card>

::: tip[]
For production use, we recommend using the `callBackUrl` parameter to receive automatic notifications when generation completes, rather than polling the status endpoint.
:::

fields.name: aspect_ratio

fields.name: resolution
fields.description: The output resolution tier. `1K` is the faster option; `2K` produces four times the pixels and takes longer. Only `1K` and `2K` are accepted — with any other value, including `4K`, the request is rejected.

fields.name: background
fields.description: Background type. transparent outputs a PNG or WebP with a real alpha channel and cannot be used with JPEG. When using transparent, describe only the subject — prompts that mention a background, scene, surface, etc. may produce a non-transparent result.

fields.name: output_format
fields.description: The output image format. `png` (default) and `webp` both carry an alpha channel and can be used with `background: transparent`. `jpeg` has no alpha channel and cannot be combined with a transparent background.

fields.name: enhance_prompt
fields.description: Rewrites the prompt into a fuller scene description before generating, which noticeably improves quality. Enabled by default (also when the parameter is omitted); pass false to turn it off.

fields.name: seed
fields.description: The random seed. Omit it to generate with a random seed. Passing the same seed together with the same prompt and parameters reproduces the same image within the same service version.

fields.name: nsfw_checker
fields.description: Defaults to false. When false, no additional content filtering is applied and results are returned directly by the model.

fields.name: image_urls
fields.description: Reference images, given as an array of 1 to 10 http(s) URLs. Required. The order of the array is the order the prompt refers to ("the first image", "the second image"). JPEG, PNG and WebP are supported, up to 30MB and 25MP each, and every URL must be directly retrievable with a GET. If an image URL cannot be fetched, the task fails with failCode 400. With more than 10 entries the request is rejected. The more references you supply the less detail each individual one keeps, so stay within 4 when fidelity matters. When combining several people or objects into a single picture, a landscape ratio such as `3:2` or `16:9` usually gives better results.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: The prompt describing the result you want. Required. Any language is supported, up to 5000 characters; if it is longer, the request is rejected. When `mask_url` is supplied, use it to describe what should be generated inside the white area of the mask.
fields.example: Replace the backpack in the first image with the colour scheme from the second image, and leave everything else unchanged

fields.name: mask_url
fields.description: Inpainting mask that switches the request into local-edit mode. A black and white image where **white marks the area to change and black is kept unchanged**, with a few pixels of feathering along the boundary. It must be used with exactly one entry in `image_urls`, otherwise the request is rejected. The mask should have the same aspect ratio as that reference image; a mask of a different size is scaled to it. In local-edit mode the output ratio follows the reference image, so `aspect_ratio` and `enhance_prompt` are ignored. It cannot be combined with `background: transparent`; such a request is rejected.

fields.name: aspect_ratio
fields.description: Output aspect ratio. Defaults to `auto`, which takes the aspect ratio of the first reference image and snaps it to the nearest supported ratio. The actual pixel size also depends on `resolution`. Ignored in local-edit mode.

fields.name: resolution
fields.description: Output resolution tier. `1K` is the faster option; `2K` produces four times the pixels and takes considerably longer, up to about 3 minutes with reference images. Only `1K` and `2K` are accepted — with any other value, including `4K`, the request is rejected.

fields.name: background
fields.description: Background type. transparent outputs a PNG or WebP with a real alpha channel and cannot be used with JPEG. When using transparent, describe only the subject — prompts that mention a background, scene, surface, etc. may produce a non-transparent result.

fields.name: output_format
fields.description: Output image format. `png` (default) and `webp` both carry an alpha channel and can be used with `background: transparent`. `jpeg` has no alpha channel and cannot be combined with a transparent background.

fields.name: enhance_prompt
fields.description: Rewrites the prompt into a fuller scene description before generating, which noticeably improves quality. Enabled by default (also when the parameter is omitted); pass false to turn it off.

fields.name: seed
fields.description: The random seed. Omit it to generate with a random seed. Passing the same seed together with the same prompt and parameters reproduces the same image within the same service version.

fields.name: nsfw_checker
fields.description: Defaults to false. When false, no additional content filtering is applied and results are returned directly by the model.

https://docs.kie.ai/market/kie/image-ups.description:
Upscale an image by `1x`, `2x`, `4x`, or `8x` while keeping the original aspect ratio. Detail is restored generatively, and text regions are upscaled with a fidelity pass so the text is never rewritten.

`upscale_factor` multiplies both width and height. `1` enhances quality at the same size (denoise, sharpen, preserve text) without changing dimensions.

## Input limits

- Publicly downloadable HTTP(S) image URL
- File size ≤ 20 MB
- Formats: JPG, PNG, WEBP, GIF (first frame only)

## Output limits

- Output total pixels ≤ 67,108,864 (67 MP, about 8192×8192), and each side ≤ 16,384 px
- The limit is checked at submission: if `input width × input height × upscale_factor²` exceeds it, the request is rejected with **422** and no task is created or charged. Lower `upscale_factor` and retry

| Input | upscale_factor | Output | Output MP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024×1024 | `1` | 1024×1024 | 1.05 |
| 1024×1024 | `2` (default) | 2048×2048 | 4.19 |
| 1024×1024 | `4` | 4096×4096 | 16.78 |
| 1024×1024 | `8` | 8192×8192 | 67.11 |
| 1646×1646 | `8` | — | 173 → 422 |

## Output

- Output width and height = input width and height × `upscale_factor` (exact integers, nothing is cropped)
- Format follows the input: JPG → JPG, WEBP → WEBP, everything else → PNG. Transparent backgrounds are filled with white
- Result URL expires after about 14 days — download and store it if you need it longer

## Billing tiers

Each task is billed once by the total output pixels:

| Tier | Output total pixels |
|---|---|
| 2K | ≤ 4.19 MP |
| 4K | ≤ 16.78 MP |
| 8K | ≤ 67.11 MP |

`1` (same-size enhancement) is tiered by the input size. For current prices, see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing).

Submit with `model=kie/image-upscale` on the unified task endpoint.

https://docs.kie.ai/market/minimax-h3/te.description:
Generate an image from a text prompt with MiniMax-H3-Image.

Prompt expansion is on by default; we recommend keeping it on for better image quality.

## Output size

**Tier + ratio** — `resolution` (default `2K`) sets the size tier and `aspect_ratio` sets the shape. `auto` lets the prompt rewriter choose the ratio based on your content (falls back to `1:1` when `expand_prompt` is `false`).

| Aspect ratio | 1K | 2K | 4K |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1:1 | 1024×1024 | 2048×2048 | 4096×4096 |
| 5:4 / 4:5 | 1152×912 / 912×1152 | 2304×1824 / 1824×2304 | 4576×3648 / 3648×4576 |
| 4:3 / 3:4 | 1184×880 / 880×1184 | 2368×1760 / 1760×2368 | 4736×3552 / 3552×4736 |
| 3:2 / 2:3 | 1248×832 / 832×1248 | 2496×1664 / 1664×2496 | 5024×3360 / 3360×5024 |
| 16:9 / 9:16 | 1360×768 / 768×1360 | 2720×1536 / 1536×2720 | 5472×3072 / 3072×5472 |
| 21:9 | 1568×672 | 3136×1344 | 6272×2688 |

**Custom size** — `width` and `height` in pixels (1–8192 each), e.g. `width: 1920, height: 1080`. Total pixels 655,360–20,000,000, width : height between 1:3 and 3:1; the output is exactly this size. When using them, do not pass `resolution` or `aspect_ratio` — this combination is not accepted.

**Which one applies**

| You pass | Output size and billing tier |
|---|---|
| Both `width` and `height` (and no `resolution` / `aspect_ratio`) | Output is `width` × `height`, billed by total pixels (≤ 1.2 MP → `1K`, ≤ 4.5 MP → `2K`, otherwise `4K`) |
| Only one of them | Not allowed: `width` and `height` must be set together |
| Neither | `resolution` (default `2K`) and `aspect_ratio` (default `auto`) apply |
| `width`/`height` together with `resolution` or `aspect_ratio` | Not allowed: the request is rejected |

- One image per task, PNG (default) or JPEG
- Billed per image by tier (`1K` / `2K` / `4K`): from `width` × `height` when both are set, otherwise from `resolution`; the tier does not depend on the ratio chosen by `auto`. For current prices, see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing)
- Result URLs expire after about 14 days — download and store them if you need them longer

Create a new image generation or editing task using the Flux Kontext AI model.

### Usage Modes
1. **Text-to-Image Generation**
   - Provide `prompt` and `aspect_ratio`
   - Model will generate a new image based on the text description

2. **Image Editing**
   - Provide `prompt` and `input_image`
   - You can optionally provide an `aspect_ratio`.  
      - If supplied, the output will be cropped or padded to match this ratio.  
      - If omitted, the original image's ratio will be preserved.
   - Model will edit the input image according to the prompt

### Important Notes
- Generated images will expire after 14 days
- Prompts only support English
- Use input.model to choose flux-kontext-pro or flux-kontext-max:
  - flux-kontext-pro: Standard model for most use cases
  - flux-kontext-max: Enhanced model for complex scenes

|---|---|---|---|
| 1:1 | 1024×1024 | 2048×2048 | 4096×4096 |

| 3:2 / 2:3 | 1248×832 / 832×1248 | 2496×1664 / 1664×2496 | 5024×3360 / 3360×5024 |
| 16:9 / 9:16 | 1360×768 / 768×1360 | 2720×1536 / 1536×2720 | 5472×3072 / 3072×5472 |
| 21:9 | 1568×672 | 3136×1344 | 6272×2688 |

**Custom size** — `width` and `height` in pixels (1–8192 each), e.g. `width: 1920, height: 1080`. Total pixels 655,360–20,000,000, width : height between 1:3 and 3:1; the output is exactly this size. When using them, do not pass `resolution` or `aspect_ratio` — this combination is not accepted.

**Which one applies**

| You pass | Output size and billing tier |
|---|---|
| Both `width` and `height` (and no `resolution` / `aspect_ratio`) | Output is `width` × `height`, billed by total pixels (≤ 1.2 MP → `1K`, ≤ 4.5 MP → `2K`, otherwise `4K`) |
| Only one of them | Not allowed: `width` and `height` must be set together |
| Neither | `resolution` (default `2K`) and `aspect_ratio` (default `auto`) apply |

- One image per task, PNG (default) or JPEG

The tier comes from `width` × `height` when both are set, otherwise from `resolution`; it does not depend on the ratio chosen by `auto`. ## File Upload Requirements

Before using the Motion Control API, you need to upload your image and video files:

<Steps>
<Step title="Upload Reference Image">
  Use the File Upload API to upload your reference image showing the subject.

  <Card title="File Upload API" icon="lucide-upload" href="/file-upload-api/quickstart">
    Learn how to upload images and get file URLs
  </Card>

  **Requirements:**
  - **File Type**: JPEG, PNG, or JPG format
  - **Max File Size**: 10MB per file, size needs to be greater than 340px, aspect ratio 2:5 to 5:2.
  - **Content**: Clear image showing the subject's head, shoulders, and torso
</Step>

<Step title="Upload Motion Video">
  Upload a video that defines the motion pattern you want to apply.

  **Requirements:**
  - **File Type**: MP4, or QuickTime format
  - **Duration**: Between 3-30 seconds per video
  - **Max File Size**: 100MB per file, size needs to be greater than 340px, aspect ratio 2:5 to 5:2.
  - **Content**: Video clearly showing the subject's head, shoulders, and torso
</Step>

<Step title="Get File URLs">
  After upload, you'll receive file URLs that you can use in the `input_urls` and `video_urls` parameters.
</Step>
</Steps>

::: warning[]
- Supported image formats: JPEG, PNG, JPG (Max: 10MB), size needs to be greater than 340px, aspect ratio 2:5 to 5:2.
- Supported video formats: MP4, QuickTime (Max: 100MB, 3-30 seconds), size needs to be greater than 340px, aspect ratio 2:5 to 5:2.
- Videos must clearly show the subject's head, shoulders, and torso
- Maximum one image and one video per request
:::

https://docs.kie.ai/market/kling/kling-3.description:
Generate high-quality videos with advanced multi-shot capabilities and element references using Kling 3.0 AI 

## Overview

Kling 3.0 is an advanced video generation model that supports both single-shot and multi-shot video creation with element references. It offers three modes: std, pro and 4K, with different resolution options, and supports sound effects for enhanced video output.

## Key Features

- **Multiple Generation Modes**: Choose between `std` (standard resolution), `pro` (higher resolution), and `4K` (ultra-high resolution) modes
- **Multi-Shot Support**: Create videos with multiple shots, each with its own prompt and duration
- **Element Reference**: Use the `@element_name` syntax to reference image/video/audio elements within prompts
- **Native Audio**: Speech, sound effects and ambience
- **Flexible Aspect Ratios**: Support for 16:9, 9:16, and 1:1 aspect ratios
- **Configurable Duration**: Video duration from 3 to 15 seconds

:::tip
In std and pro modes, enabling sound costs more. In multi-shot mode, billing is based on the sum of the shot durations. For current prices, see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing).
:::

## Resolution Mappings

The resolution depends on both the `mode` and `aspect_ratio` parameters:

<Tabs groupId="mode">
<TabItem value="std" label="Standard Mode (std)">

| Aspect Ratio | Resolution |
|--------------|------------|
| 16:9         | 1280×720   |
| 9:16         | 720×1280   |
| 1:1          | 720×720    |

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="pro" label="Pro Mode (pro)">

| Aspect Ratio | Resolution |
|--------------|------------|
| 16:9         | 1920×1080  |
| 9:16         | 1080×1920  |
| 1:1          | 1440×1440  |

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="4K" label="4K Mode (4K)">

| Aspect Ratio | Resolution |
|--------------|------------|
| 16:9         | 3840×2160  |
| 9:16         | 2160×3840  |
| 1:1          | 2160×2160  |

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

:::info[]
4K mode provides higher resolution output but may take longer to generate and consume more credits.
:::

## Single-Shot vs Multi-Shot Mode

### Single-Shot Mode (`multi_shots: false`)
- Uses the main `prompt` field for video generation
- Supports first and last frame images via `image_urls`
- Sound effects are optional

### Multi-Shot Mode (`multi_shots: true`)
- Uses `multi_prompt` array to define multiple shots
- Each shot has its own prompt and duration (1-12 seconds)
- Only supports first frame image (via `image_urls[0]`)
- The maximum number of characters per shot is 500


## Aspect Ratio Auto-Adaptation

When you provide `image_urls` (first and/or last frame images), the `aspect_ratio` parameter becomes optional. The system will automatically adapt the aspect ratio based on the uploaded images, so you don't need to specify it manually.

:::tip[]
If you upload reference images, you can omit the `aspect_ratio` parameter and let the system automatically match the aspect ratio of your images.
:::

## Element References

You can reference element in your prompts using the `@element_name` syntax. Define elements in the `kling_elements` array:

- **Image Elements**: 2-4 image URLs (JPG/PNG, max 10MB each)
- **Video Elements**: Up to 1 video URL (MP4/MOV format, the video duration must be at least 3 seconds, and the effective segment length should be between 3 and 8 seconds)
- **Audio Reference**: Up to 1 audio URL (audio duration must be between 5 and 30 seconds)

:::tip[]
Use descriptive element names and ensure the element name in `kling_elements` matches the name used in your prompt (without the @ symbol).
A single task can reference a maximum of 3 elements, and each `@element` will occupy 37 characters.
:::

## File Upload Requirements

Before using element references, upload your image  files:

### 1. Upload Files

Use the File Upload API to upload your source images.

:::info[File Upload API]
Learn how to upload files and get file URLs: [File Upload API Quickstart](/file-upload-api/quickstart)
:::

### 2. Get File URLs

After upload, you'll receive file URLs that you can use in `element_input_urls` and `element_input_audio_urls`.

:::caution[]
- formats: 
    - Image (JPG, PNG, max 10MB per file, 2-4 files per element)
    - Video (MP4, MOV format. Video duration should be at least 3 seconds. The effective video segment length should be between 3 and 8 seconds)
    - Audio (Audio duration must be between 5 and 30 seconds)
- Ensure file URLs are accessible and not expired
:::

https://docs.kie.ai/market/kling/v4-refe.description:
Generate videos with Kling 4.0 from reference images, reference videos, elements, and voices. Reference your materials in the prompt using `@image_1`, `@video_1`, or custom `@name` tags.

## Materials and References

All four material types are optional. When none are provided, the request behaves as plain text-to-video. Once provided, reference them in `prompt` as shown below:

| Material | Reference syntax | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Reference images `images` | `@image_1`, `@image_2`, … | 10 images |
| Reference videos `videos` | `@video_1`, `@video_2`, … | 5 videos, each 2–30 seconds |
| Elements `elements` |
- Reference videos and video elements combined are limited to 5; all four material types combined are limited to 15.
- An image element requires 2–4 images, with the first one as the primary shot; a video element requires one 3–8 second single-shot character video.
- Custom names must be 1–20 characters of Chinese characters, letters, digits, or underscores, must be unique (case-insensitive), and must not use reserved names such as `image_N`, `video_N`, `first_frame`, or `last_frame`.
- Referencing an undeclared material returns a parameter error and the task is not created.

::: tip[]
When `aspect_ratio` is omitted, the ratio adapts to your materials if any are provided, and falls back to `16:9` when none are. When `videos` is provided, `keep_original_sound` controls whether the original audio is kept; when `videos` is omitted, native audio is enabled by default.
:::

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Video description. Required. Maximum 8000 characters. Use `@` to mention assets uploaded in this request: - `@image_1`, `@image_2`, … map to `image_urls` in order (1-based) - `@video_1`, `@video_2`, … map to `video_urls` - `@name` maps to the `name` of an item in `elements` or `voices` Every `@` mention must match an asset included in this request, otherwise the request is rejected. Mentions use longest-match against declared names. If the matched name ends with a letter, digit, or underscore, the next character cannot be a letter, digit, or underscore.
fields.example: @Hero sits at the desk in @video_1, picks up the doll from @image_1, and greets using @Narrator

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Output video duration in seconds. Integer from 3 to 30. Default: `5`.

fields.name: resolution
fields.description: Output resolution. `720p` or `1080p`. Default: `720p`.

fields.name: aspect_ratio
fields.description: Output aspect ratio. Optional. - If omitted and any reference asset is provided, the model uses `auto` - If omitted and no reference asset is provided, the model uses `16:9`

fields.name: image_urls
fields.description: Reference images, up to 10 publicly accessible URLs. Mention them in the prompt as `@image_1`, `@image_2`, … in array order. Each side must be 300–65536 pixels; aspect ratio 0.40–2.5.

fields.name: video_urls
fields.description: Reference videos, up to 5 clips, each 2–30 seconds. Mention them in the prompt as `@video_1`, `@video_2`, …. Reference videos plus video subjects in `elements` cannot exceed 5 in total.

fields.name: keep_original_sound
fields.description: Whether to keep the original audio of the reference videos. Only takes effect when `video_urls` is provided. Default: `false`. If no reference video is provided, native audio is always generated.

fields.name: elements
fields.description: Subjects used only for this task. Up to 7 items, of which at most 3 can be video subjects. Mention them in the prompt as `@name`. `image_urls`, `video_urls`, `elements`, and `voices` together cannot exceed 15 items.

fields.name: voices
fields.description: Standalone voice references used only for this task. Up to 3 items. Mention them in the prompt as `@name`. Audio bound on a subject via `voice_url` is separate and does not count toward this quota.

> **Note**
>
> *   **Image-to-Video (First Frame)**, **Image-to-Video (First & Last Frames)**, and **Multimodal Reference-to-Video** (including reference images, videos, and audio) are three mutually exclusive scenarios and **cannot be used simultaneously**.
> *   Multimodal Reference-to-Video can indirectly achieve a "First/Last Frame + Multimodal Reference" effect by specifying reference images as the first or last frame via prompts. If you need to strictly guarantee that the first and last frames are identical to the specified images, **prioritize using Image-to-Video (First & Last Frames)**

https://docs.kie.ai/market/kling/v4-flas.description:
Generate videos with Kling 4.0 Flash from reference images, reference videos, and elements. Mention your materials in the prompt using `@image_1`, `@video_1`, or custom `@name` tags. Standalone `voices` is not supported; bind character audio on the element's `voice_url`. Try it online and see pricing on the [Kling 4.0 Flash API page](https://kie.ai/kling-4-0-flash).

## Materials and References

All three material types are optional. When none are provided, the request behaves as plain text-to-video. Once provided, mention them in `prompt` as shown below:

| Material | Mention syntax | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| Reference images `image_urls` | `@image_1`, `@image_2`, … | 10 images |
| Reference videos `video_urls` | `@video_1`, `@video_2`, … | 5 videos |
| Elements `elements` | `@name` | 7 items, of which at most 3 can be video elements |

- Reference videos plus video elements cannot exceed 5 in total. The three material types combined cannot exceed 15.
- Combined duration of all reference videos and video elements must be 2–20 seconds. If it is outside that range, the completion callback returns a failure.
- An image element needs 2–4 images, with the first as the primary view. A video element needs one 3–8 second single-shot character video.
- Custom names must be 1–20 characters of Chinese characters, letters, digits, or underscores; unique (case-insensitive); and must not use reserved names such as `image_N`, `video_N`, `keyframe_N`, `object_N`, `audio_N`, `first_frame`, or `last_frame`.
- Mentioning an undeclared material is rejected immediately and the task is not created.
- Output resolution is always `720p`. Duration is 3–20 seconds.

::: tip[]
When `aspect_ratio` is omitted, the model uses `auto` if any reference material is provided, and `16:9` when none are. When `video_urls` is provided, `keep_original_sound` controls whether the original audio is kept.
:::

Use this endpoint to create a new image-to-video generation task.

- First-frame-to-video: provide `first_frame_url` only
- First-and-last-frame-to-video: provide both `first_frame_url` and `last_frame_url`
- Video continuation: provide `first_clip_url`

Transform existing videos into enhanced dynamic content using Runway's advanced Aleph AI model. This endpoint enables precise video-to-video generation through text-guided transformations, perfect for creating enhanced visual content from existing videos.

:::highlight purple
The Runway Aleph API requires a text prompt and reference video URL to generate transformed videos. The AI will modify and enhance the provided video based on your text description.
:::

Create dynamic AI-generated videos from text prompts or image references.

### Usage Guide
- Create short videos (5-10 seconds) using AI visualization
- Generate videos based on text descriptions or reference images
- Suitable for social media content, digital art, or concept visualization


### Parameter Details
- `prompt` describes what you want to show in the video
- `image_url` provides visual reference for AI
- `aspect_ratio` determines video orientation (vertical or horizontal)
- `duration` control the video duration (5 or 10 seconds), where if a 10-second video is selected, 1080p resolution cannot be selected 
- `quality` video resolution (720p or 1080p), where if 1080p is selected, 10-second video cannot be generated
- `watermark` video watermark text content, empty string means no watermark

### Developer Notes
- Generated videos are stored for 14 days before automatic deletion
-  For text-only generation, aspect ratio must be explicitly specified

Extend existing AI-generated videos to create longer sequences. The result is a single video containing the original clip followed by the continuation (about 5 seconds longer than the source).

### Usage Guide
- Add additional segments to your AI-generated videos
- Maintain visual consistency while extending narratives
- Create longer sequences for storytelling or demonstrations


### Parameter Details
- `task_id` identifies the original video to extend
- `prompt` guides how the video should continue
- `quality` video resolution, optional values are 720p or 1080p. 
- `watermark` video watermark text content, empty string means no watermark

### Developer Notes
- Extended videos are stored for 14 days before automatic deletion
- Extension maintains the same aspect ratio as the original video
- Extension works best when continuing the same subject/theme as the original video

### Generation modes

Choose one mode per request, based on whether you send a first frame or a video:

| Mode | When | `duration` | Other assets allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| A Text / reference images / characters | No `first_frame_url`, no `video_list` | **Required**, integer **3–15** | `image_urls`, `character_ids` |
| B First frame only | `first_frame_url` set, no `last_frame_url` | **Required**, integer **3–15** | None (see exclusions) |
| C First and last frame | Both `first_frame_url` and `last_frame_url` | **Required**, integer **3–10** | None (see exclusions) |
| D Video edit | `video_list` set | **Do not send** | `image_urls`, `character_ids` |

**Exclusions** (when `first_frame_url` or `last_frame_url` is set):

- Do not send `last_frame_url` alone
- Do not send `image_urls`, `video_list`, or `character_ids` at the same time

**Total Quota Overview:**
The system utilizes a quota-based system for content uploads. The total available capacity is **7 units**. Different parameters consume different amounts of this quota. Please ensure the sum of all consumed units does not exceed 7.

**Quota Consumption Rules:**
1.  **Images (`image_urls`)**: Each image consumes **1 unit**.
2.  **Videos (`video_list`)**: Each video consumes **2 units**.
    *   *Note: Maximum of 1 video per request.*
3.  **Character IDs (`character_ids`)**: Each ID consumes **1 unit**.
    *   *Note: Maximum of 3 character IDs per request.*

**Constraint Formula:**
`(Number of Images) + (Number of Videos × 2) + (Number of Character IDs) ≤ 7`

**Example Scenarios:**
*   If 1 video (2 units) and 3 Character IDs (3 units) are uploaded, you can upload a maximum of 2 additional images.
*   If no video or Character IDs are provided, you can upload up to 7 images.

**Note — first-frame mode:** when first_frame_url is set, image_urls, video_list, character_ids and audio_ids cannot be used.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: The video prompt, used to describe the visual content, style, cinematography, or character actions of the target video.
fields.example: Generate a short video of a futuristic city at night, with the camera slowly pushing forward as a character emerges from a neon-lit street.

fields.name: image_urls
fields.description: An array of image URLs. Multiple reference images can be uploaded to provide references for characters, scenes, styles, or storyboards. Image limitations: - Each file must not exceed `20MB` - Use publicly accessible image URLs - Maximum of 7 images - Note: This field is mutually exclusive with the first-frame image (`first_frame_url`) and cannot be provided at the same time.

fields.name: first_frame_url
fields.description: The URL of the first-frame image. Used to specify the starting frame of the generated video. Note: This field is mutually exclusive with `image_urls`, `audio_ids`, `video_list`, and `character_ids` and cannot be provided at the same time.

fields.name: last_frame_url
fields.description: The URL of the last-frame image. Used to specify the ending frame of the generated video. Note: The last-frame image cannot be used alone and must be provided together with the first-frame image (`first_frame_url`).

fields.name: audio_ids
fields.description: An array of audio IDs generated by the `gemini-omni-audio` interface. Used to provide narration, dialogue, background music, or sound references for the video. Up to 3 items. Note: This field is mutually exclusive with the first-frame image (`first_frame_url`) and cannot be provided at the same time.

fields.name: video_list
fields.description: An array of video clips. Each element describes a video asset that can be used for generation and its trimming time range. Video limitations: - Each file must not exceed `100MB` - Video duration must not exceed `30s` - `ends` should be greater than `start` - The difference between the end and start times must not exceed `10s` - Maximum of 1 item, occupying two image slots - Note: This field is mutually exclusive with the first-frame image (`first_frame_url`) and cannot be provided at the same time.

fields.name: character_ids
fields.description: An array of character IDs generated by the `gemini-omni-character` interface. Used to provide character appearance, identity, or person references for the video. Up to 3 character IDs. Each uses 1 image slot (2 if created with portrait + body images). Total slots (images + videos × 2 + character slots) ≤ 7. Note: This field is mutually exclusive with the first-frame image (`first_frame_url`) and cannot be provided at the same time.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: The duration of the generated video, in seconds. Valid values are 4, 6, 8, and 10. This parameter only takes effect when there is no video input. If video input is used, the output duration is determined by the model, and the `duration` parameter will be ignored. Note: When video input is provided, the output duration is automatically determined by the model. In this case, the `duration` parameter will not take effect.

fields.name: aspect_ratio
fields.description: The aspect ratio of the generated video. `16:9` is landscape, and `9:16` is portrait.

fields.name: resolution
fields.description: The resolution of the generated video. Valid values are 360p, 720p, 1080p, and 4k.

fields.name: seed
fields.description: The random seed. Valid range: [0, 2147483647]. If not specified, the system will automatically generate a seed. A fixed seed can improve result reproducibility, but because the model itself is stochastic, results may still vary.

### Usage notes

- You can only extend from the end of the video. You cannot prepend or insert in the middle
- The result is a complete video. Duration is about source length + `duration`. You do not need to stitch clips yourself
- The source video must be **15 seconds or shorter**. A successful extend returns a new `taskId`. If the resulting video is still 15 seconds or shorter, you can use that ID to extend again
- Source resolution must be **360p** or **720p** (1080p / 4k is not supported yet)
- The model mainly uses the ending of the source video as context. If a person or object only appeared earlier, describe it again in the prompt, or pass a reference image

fields.description: ID of the source task to extend. Required. Must be a completed `google/gemini-omni-flash-1-2` generation task, or a completed `google/gemini-omni-flash-1-2-extend` extend task. The source video must be 360p or 720p (1080p / 4k is not supported yet) and no longer than 15 seconds.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: Extend prompt. Required and must be non-empty. Describe what happens next, such as action, camera, environment, and sound. Put anything you do not want in the prompt as well.
fields.example: The scene continues: the robot turns to the camera and waves, the camera slowly pulls back.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: How many seconds to extend from the end. Required. Integer **3–10**. This is the length of the new segment, not the full output. Full duration is about source length + `duration`.

fields.name: image_urls
fields.description: Reference image URLs, max **3**. Used to keep people and objects consistent. Limits: - Use publicly accessible image URLs - Supported formats: png / jpeg / webp - Each file must be no larger than `20MB`

The generated video is returned in MP4 format at 25 fps. The final output duration follows the audio duration: if the source video is longer than the audio, it will be trimmed; if the source video is shorter than the audio, it will be looped.

https://docs.kie.ai/market/kie/video-ups.description:
Upscale a source video to `1080P`, `2K`, or `4K` while keeping the original aspect ratio, frame rate, frame count, and audio.

`resolution` is an **output box**. The source is fitted into the selected box until one side meets the edge; the picture is not cropped. If the source is larger than that box, it is scaled down to the box and enhanced; if it already matches the box, it is enhanced at the same size. The output always matches the box you select.

## Input limits

- Publicly downloadable HTTP(S) video URL
- File size ≤ 50 MB
- Duration ≤ 60 seconds
- Accepted formats: MP4, MOV, and MKV
- Duration and file size are validated after download, so over-limit videos fail the task rather than the submit request

## Output

| resolution | Landscape box | Portrait box |
|---|---|---|
| `1080P` | 1920×1080 | 1080×1920 |
| `2K` (default) | 2560×1440 | 1440×2560 |
| `4K` | 3840×2160 | 2160×3840 |

- Container: MP4 (H.264 + AAC). Audio is preserved when the source has a soundtrack
- Width and height are always even
- Result URL expires after about 14 days — download and store it if you need it longer
- Processing time scales with frame count and output pixels (a ~8s 1080p clip to 2K is typically around 30–40 seconds of processing, excluding queue)

## Create Task

Submit with `model=video/upscale` on the unified task endpoint.

### Veo 3.1 Generation API

Our **Veo 3.1 Generation API** is more than a direct wrapper around Google's baseline. It layers extensive optimisation and reliability tooling on top of the official models, giving you greater flexibility and markedly higher success rates (see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing) for full details).

| Capability | Details |
| :------------------- | :------ |
| **Models** | • **Veo 3.1 Quality** — flagship model, highest fidelity• **Veo 3.1 Fast** — cost-efficient variant that still delivers strong visual results• **Veo 3.1 Lite** — most cost-effective model for high-volume generation |
| **Tasks** | • **Text → Video**• **Image → Video** (single reference frame or first and last frames)• **Material → Video** (based on material images) |
| **Generation Modes** | • **TEXT\_2\_VIDEO** — Text-to-video: using text prompts only• **FIRST\_AND\_LAST\_FRAMES\_2\_VIDEO** — First and last frames to video: generate transition videos using one or two images• **REFERENCE\_2\_VIDEO** — Material-to-video: based on material images (**Fast model** and **Lite model**, supports **16:9 & 9:16**) |
| **Aspect Ratios** | Supports both native **16:9** and **9:16** outputs. **Auto** mode lets the system decide aspect ratio based on input materials and internal strategy (for production control, we recommend explicitly setting `aspect_ratio`). |
| **Output Quality** | Both **16:9** and **9:16** support **1080P** and **4K** outputs.|
| **Audio Track** | All videos ship with background audio by default. In rare cases, audio may be suppressed when the scene is deemed sensitive (e.g. minors). |

### Why our Veo 3.1 API is different

1. **True vertical video** – Native Veo 3.1 supports **9:16** output, delivering authentic vertical videos without the need for re-framing or manual editing.
2. **Global language reach** – Our flow supports multilingual prompts by default (no extra configuration required).
3. **Significant cost savings** – see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing) for current prices.

:::tip
Choosing 1080p or 4k at generation costs the 720p price plus the 1080P / 4K upgrade price. For current prices, see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing).
:::

::: info[]
  Extend an existing Veo 3.1 video by generating new content based on the original video and a text prompt. This feature allows you to extend video duration or add new content based on your existing video clips.
:::

The result (resultUrls) is the newly generated continuation clip (720p) that starts from the last frame of the source video. The callback additionally includes info.fullResultUrls with the source and the continuation stitched together.

Our **Veo 3.1 Video Extension API** is more than simple video splicing. It layers intelligent extension algorithms on top of the official models, giving you greater flexibility and markedly higher success rates (see [pricing details](https://kie.ai/pricing) for full details).

| Capability              | Details |
| :---------------------- | :------ |
| **Smart Extension**     | Generate new video segments based on existing videos and text prompts |
| **Seamless Connection** | Extended videos naturally connect with the original video |
| **Flexible Control**    | Precisely control the style and actions of extended content through prompts |
| **High-Quality Output** | Maintain the same quality and style as the original video |
| **Audio Track**         | Extended videos default to background audio, consistent with the original video |

### Why our Veo 3.1 Video Extension is different

1. **Smart Content Understanding** – Deeply understands the content and style of the original video to ensure coherence of extended content.
2. **Natural Transition** – Extended video segments seamlessly connect with the original video without visible splicing marks.
3. **Flexible Control** – Precisely control the actions, scenes, and styles of extended content through detailed prompts.
4. **Significant Cost Savings** – see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing) for current prices.

:::tip
Choosing 1080p or 4k at generation costs the 720p price plus the 1080P / 4K upgrade price. For current prices, see [kie.ai/pricing](https://kie.ai/pricing).
:::

***

### Video Extension Workflow

The video extension feature is based on your existing Veo3.1 generated videos and works through the following steps:

1. **Provide Original Video**: Use the `taskId` from the original video generation task
2. **Describe Extension Content**: Use `prompt` to detail how you want the video to be extended
3. **Smart Analysis**: The system analyzes the content, style, and actions of the original video
4. **Generate Extension**: Generate new video segments based on analysis results and your prompts
5. **Seamless Connection**: Naturally connect the extended video with the original video

### Extension Features

::: info[Through the video extension feature, you can:]
- Extend video duration and add more content
- Change video direction and add new actions or scenes
- Add new elements while maintaining the original style
- Create richer video stories
:::

**Extension Features:**

- **Smart Analysis**: Deeply understand the content and style of the original video
- **Natural Connection**: Extended content seamlessly connects with the original video
- **Flexible Control**: Precisely control extended content through prompts
- **Quality Assurance**: Maintain the same quality and style as the original video

::: warning[**Important Notes**]
- Can only extend videos generated through the Veo3.1 API
- Extended content must also comply with platform content policies
- Recommend using English prompts for best results
- Video extension consumes credits, see [pricing Details](https://kie.ai/pricing) for specific pricing
:::

### Best Practices

::: tip[Prompt Writing Suggestions]
1. **Detailed Action Description**: Clearly describe how you want the video to be extended, e.g., "the dog continues running through the park, jumping over obstacles"
2. **Maintain Style Consistency**: Ensure the style of extended content matches the original video
3. **Natural Transition**: Described actions should naturally connect with the end of the original video
4. **Use English**: Recommend using English prompts for best results
5. **Avoid Conflicts**: Ensure extended content doesn't create logical conflicts with the original video
:::

::: tip[Technical Recommendations]
1. **Use Callbacks**: Strongly recommend using callback mechanisms to get results in production environments
2. **Download Promptly**: Download video files promptly after generation, URLs have time limits
3. **Error Handling**: Implement appropriate error handling and retry mechanisms
4. **Credit Management**: Monitor credit usage to ensure sufficient balance
5. **Seed Control**: Use the seeds parameter to control the randomness of generated content
:::

## Important Notes

::: warning[Important Limitations]
- **Original Video Requirements**: Can only extend videos generated through the Veo3.1 API
- **Content Policy**: Extended content must also comply with platform content policies
- **Credit Consumption**: Video extension consumes credits, see [pricing Details](https://kie.ai/pricing) for specific pricing
- **Processing Time**: Video extension may take several minutes to over ten minutes to process
- **URL Validity**: Generated video URLs have time limits, please download and save promptly
:::

::: note[Extended Video Features]
- **Seamless Connection**: Extended videos will naturally connect with the original video
- **Quality Maintenance**: Extended videos maintain the same quality as the original video
- **Style Consistency**: Extended content will maintain the visual style of the original video
- **Flexible Control**: Prompts can precisely control the content and direction of extension
:::

## Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Common Error Handling">
- **404 Error**: Check that task_id is a successful Veo 3.1 task.
- **400 Error**: Check if the prompt complies with content policies
- **402 Error**: Confirm the account has sufficient credits
- **500 Error**: Temporary server issue, please try again later
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Extension Quality Issues">
- **Unnatural Connection**: Try more detailed prompt descriptions
- **Style Inconsistency**: Ensure the prompt includes style descriptions
- **Disconnected Actions**: Check if action descriptions in the prompt are reasonable
- **Content Deviation**: Adjust prompts to more accurately describe desired extension content
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Technical Issues">
- **Callback Receipt Failure**: Check if the callback URL is accessible
- **Video Download Failure**: Confirm URL validity and network connection
- **Abnormal Task Status**: Use the details query interface to check task status
- **Insufficient Credits**: Recharge credits promptly to continue using the service
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

### Streaming Support

When `stream: true` is set in the request, the API returns responses as server-sent events (SSE). 

**Streaming Response Format:**
- Content-Type: `text/event-stream`
- Event names include `message_start`, `content_block_start`, `content_block_delta`, `message_delta`, and `message_stop`

## Features

- Standard chat with `messages`.
- Optional stream response with Claude events.
- Optional thinking flag (`thinkingFlag`).
- **Note**:This model does not support function calls and claude code.


## Request Notes

- Put the current model name in the `model` field.
- Use `messages` for conversation history.
- Set `stream` to `true` for SSE output.

## Authentication

Authentication: send `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`. Clients that send `x-api-key` (such as the Anthropic SDK) must set it to `Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`. `anthropic-version` is optional.

Each event contains partial message content, enabling real-time display of responses in your application. **Streaming Response Format:** - Content-Type: `text/event-stream` - Each event line starts with `data: ` followed by JSON - Events contain incremental message deltas - Final event indicates completion with `finish_reason` - The stream ends with a chunk carrying usage and credits_consumed, followed by data: [DONE].   • The image_url key name remains unchanged for all file types
  • Only the url value points to your specific media file
// Example for Video/Audio/PDF/Image:
{ "type": "image_url", "image_url": { "url": "https://..." } }

fields.name: image_url
fields.description: 必填。待分离图片的 URL。 - 只能传 1 张，须为公网可访问地址 - 支持格式：JPEG、PNG、WEBP - 不超过 10 MB

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: 可选。描述要分离的元素，0–2000 字符。 - 传入时，模型按描述分离指定元素 - 留空时，模型自动识别图片中的主要元素 - 可用 `<bbox>x1 y1 x2 y2</bbox>` 标注元素位置，坐标按 0–1000 归一化
fields.example: 将标题文字 <bbox>179 58 809 197</bbox> 和鹦鹉 <bbox>330 274 641 991</bbox> 分离为独立图层

fields.name: size
fields.description: 输出图片的清晰度档位。默认 `auto`。 - `auto`：保持原图尺寸（小于 1K 提升到 1K，大于 2K 压缩到 2K），按 2K 档计费 - `1K` / `1.5K` / `2K`：固定清晰度档位

fields.name: output_format
fields.description: 底图的输出格式。默认 `png`。仅影响底图，分离出的图层固定为 PNG（透明背景）。

fields.name: max_images
fields.description: 最多输出的图片张数（含 1 张底图）。范围 2–100，默认 30。按实际返回的张数计费。

fields.name: text_recognition
fields.description: 是否识别图层中的文字。默认 `false`。

fields.name: nsfw_checker
fields.description: 默认 false。为 false 时不额外进行内容过滤，结果由模型直接返回。
